messages:
sara_sales: MedAtlas signed MSA for a 6-month enterprise commit. Need a presales capacity checklist and clarifications on reserved GPUs vs burst credits. Their traffic: steady ~120 requests/sec (gen), peak windows up to 600 rps for ~8 minutes, median prompt ~350 tokens, some long reports ~1.5k tokens. Also got an ops Q: how tolerant to instance eviction do we need to be for spot fallback? who can help with sizing + pricing impact?

ben_infra: Congrats! Quick Q — what model family are they planning to run? quantized LLM or fp16 baseline? That changes GPU memory and throughput assumptions.

sara_sales: They're planning to use an open Llama-variant (chat/structured outputs), prefer 8-bit quantized for cost. I'll confirm exact shard later.

mike_runtime: For that traffic shape + quantized model, recommend reserved baseline: 3 GPUs for steady-state, with autoscale to 9 GPUs for spikes (burst via reserved pool + spot). Reason: continuous batching + KV cache gives good steady throughput but peaks need headroom. Preheat KV cache for top 20% prompts reduces tail latency.

mike_runtime: Autoscale policy suggestion (example):
```yaml
min_replicas: 3
scale_query_per_second: 80  # scale up when avg qps per GPU > 80
scale_step: 2
max_replicas: 9
spot_fallback: true
preheat_enabled: true
kv_warmup: true
```

elaine_se: Security note for MedAtlas (HIPAA): they require BAA on file, keys in customer KMS, VPC peering + private endpoints. For Private deployment we need to include audit logs and disable spot fallback unless they permit it in questionnaire. Ask legal for exceptions.

ben_infra: Eviction tolerance: if they disallow spot or low eviction tolerance, we should size reserved pool to handle 95th percentile peak — that moves reserved from 3->7 GPUs. If they allow spot fallback with 30s retry window and queue smoothing, we can keep smaller reserved and rely on burst credits.

sara_sales: @elaine_se can you confirm whether MedAtlas's security team will accept spot fallback for non-sensitive inference (we can route PHI through dedicated reserved only)?

elaine_se: I flagged that in the questionnaire: they want all PHI-handling routes on non-preemptible hardware. We can split by routing policy: PHI->dedicated reserved, non-PHI->burst/spot. Need their endpoint mapping.

mike_runtime: Operationally, split routing is straightforward: route requests with header x-sensitivity:high to the private reserved pool. Add fallbacks so if reserved capacity exhausted we return 503 with a known retry-after or route to degraded model (smaller model) to avoid PHI leakage.

ben_infra: Pricing impact: moving from 3 reserved -> 7 reserved increases committed cost ~2.2–2.6x for reserved GPU line items (rough estimate). Burst credit model reduces committed spend but increases unit token cost during spikes. We'll run a cost simulation once we have exact token distribution.

sara_sales: OK. Action items: 1) sara_sales to confirm model shard + token distribution (owner) 2) mike_runtime to produce an autoscale + routing YAML for the split PHI/non-PHI flow by EOD tomorrow 3) ben_infra to run a month-cost sim for three scenarios (3-reserved, 5-reserved, 7-reserved) with spot fallback allowed vs disallowed 4) elaine_se to follow up on questionnaire answers re: spot for non-PHI only.

deploy-bot: preheat job scheduled for medatlas-preheat-2026-06-21 03:00 UTC (kv-cache population for top prompts).

sara_sales: Thanks everyone — ping me in this thread if you need additional telemetry from the account team or sample production prompt set. :thumbsup:
